transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi... well, what brings me in is that I’ve just been waking up with this really heavy, hollow sadness. It's... it's like the studio lights are on, but there is no music in me anymore, you know? 

The studio actually just changed all their overhead lights, by the way. They put in these terrible, harsh fluorescent bulbs in the main rehearsal space. I tried telling the owner that nobody can feel the choreography when they feel like they are in a hospital waiting room, but he just ignores me. He is always trying to cut costs since the building's rent went up last year. I even had to buy my own floor tape last week because he wouldn't order the good kind, and you really can't compromise on marley tape or someone is going to twist an ankle. I've seen it happen. 

But... yeah, I just wake up feeling so sad and empty.
How long have you been waking up with this heavy, hollow sadness?

Um... I think it's been about nine months. Yeah, nine months. Because I remember it started right around the time we were casting for the autumn showcase. Which, by the way, was a complete nightmare from the start because our lead soloist decided to move to New York with zero notice. Just packed up and left a week into rehearsals. I had to recast the entire second act in three days, and the girl who stepped up—bless her heart, she tries so hard—she just didn't have the extension for the leaps we choreographed. I had to rewrite the whole sequence to hide her weaker left leg, which totally changed the emotional arc of the piece. You spend weeks building a specific rhythm and then one person leaves and the whole ecosystem just collapses. And the costumes were late on top of it all... but, um, yeah. About nine months of feeling this way.
Do you still enjoy dancing and rehearsing, or has that changed for you over the past nine months?

I... honestly, I don't really know. I haven't really noticed if I enjoy it or not anymore, it's just... I just show up. 

But showing up is getting so annoying anyway because the floor in the main room is completely ruined right now. Someone spilled one of those massive protein shakes right in front of the center mirrors on Tuesday. And you know how impossible it is to get dried protein powder out of wood grain? It turns into literal cement. I actually used to drink those exact shakes, the vanilla pea protein ones, until the company changed the formula last summer and made it taste like chalk. My roommate tried to use my leftover powder to make these "healthy" muffins because she's on this huge fitness kick, and she completely destroyed our kitchen. She left flour and baking soda all over the counters, and the muffins were practically bricks anyway. I told her she should just stick to regular flour, you know? It's not worth ruining a good pastry just to save a few calories. 

But... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, about enjoying rehearsals. Yeah, I'm really not sure. I just feel kind of blank when I'm there.
Do you find pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, outside of dancing and rehearsing?

Um... outside of dancing? I don't know, I haven't really thought about it. I guess I haven't noticed if I enjoy other things either. 

I used to really like going to this little coffee shop down the street from my apartment, though. They had this amazing cold brew that they steeped for like 24 hours. But then they got bought out by this big chain, and they completely changed the menu. They got rid of all the good pastries, too. They used to have these incredible almond croissants that this local baker made fresh every morning. He was this older guy, Italian I think, and he would always give me an extra one if I came in right before closing. He retired last year, actually, moved to Florida or somewhere warm. Which I completely get, because the winters here are just getting ridiculous. Last February, the heating in my building went out for three whole days. I had to sleep in my winter coat and two pairs of sweatpants. The landlord tried to say it was a city issue, but I talked to the super and he said the boiler hadn't been serviced since like 2015. You really can't trust landlords to keep up with maintenance unless you're constantly on them about it. 

But, um... yeah, I don't really know if I enjoy anything else right now. I just haven't noticed.
Are there things that you used to find pleasurable or enjoyable that you still find pleasurable or enjoyable now?

Um... things I still enjoy? I don't... I can't really think of anything off the top of my head. It's hard to say if I actually enjoy things or if I'm just doing them out of habit, you know? 

Like, I still water my plants every Sunday morning. I have this huge Monstera in my living room that I've kept alive for four years. But I had to move it last week because the leaves were getting scorched by the afternoon sun. The windows in my apartment face west, and the glare off the glass building across the street is blinding from like 3 PM to sunset. They built that high-rise so fast, too. It felt like one day it was an empty lot and the next there was this massive glass eyesore blocking my view of the skyline. The construction noise was unbearable for months. They would start drilling at 6 AM, which completely ruined my sleep schedule. I tried wearing earplugs, but they always fall out in the middle of the night, and then I'd wake up to the sound of metal clanking. I actually bought one of those expensive white noise machines to try and drown it out, but the cord was too short to reach the outlet near my bed, so I had to use this ugly orange extension cord that completely ruined the aesthetic of my bedroom. 

So... wait, what was the question? Enjoyable things? Yeah, I don't really know. Nothing really stands out right now.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to care about?

I don't really know if I've lost interest, exactly. I just... I don't feel much of anything toward the things I used to care about. It's like my brain just isn't registering it. 

Which is weird, because I used to care so much about everything. Like my wardrobe, for example. I used to spend hours picking out outfits and making sure everything coordinated perfectly. I have this incredible vintage silk scarf collection that I started when I was in college. I found the first one at this tiny thrift store near campus that smelled like mothballs and old books. The owner was this sweet lady who always wore these massive, chunky turquoise necklaces. She told me the scarf belonged to a local theater actress in the 70s. I actually tried to find that thrift store again a few months ago when I was visiting a friend near my old university, but it got turned into one of those overpriced bubble tea places. They charge like eight dollars for a drink that's mostly ice anyway. I don't get the hype with bubble tea, honestly. The tapioca pearls always feel like you're chewing on rubber bands, and the straws are so wide you feel like you're going to choke. My friend ordered this taro-flavored one that was bright purple, and it looked completely radioactive. 

But, um... yeah, I don't know about losing interest. I just haven't really noticed feeling one way or the other about things lately.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from things that would normally bring you happiness?

I mean... unable to experience pleasure? That sounds so absolute. I wouldn't say I'm *unable*, it's just... I'm not really paying attention to happiness right now, I guess. 

I was thinking about happiness the other day, actually, because my sister called to tell me she's pregnant with her second kid. She sounded so thrilled, you know? They've been trying for a while. They live out in the suburbs now, in this massive house with a wraparound porch. It's beautiful, but the property taxes out there are insane. She was complaining about how much they have to pay just for the local school district, even though her oldest isn't even in kindergarten yet. He's three, and he's obsessed with dinosaurs. Like, completely obsessed. I bought him this huge plush T-Rex for his birthday, and my sister said he drags it everywhere. He even tries to feed it mashed potatoes at dinner. Which is cute, but also kind of gross because now the dinosaur has these crusty potato stains all over its face. You can't just throw something that big in the washing machine, either. You have to spot clean it, and honestly, who has the time for that? I remember when I had this white rug in my old apartment—worst mistake of my life. Someone spilled red wine on it during a cast party, and I spent three hours scrubbing it with baking soda and club soda. It never really came out, just turned into this weird, faded pink blob right in the middle of the room. I ended up having to buy a coffee table just to cover it up. 

So, um... yeah. I don't know if I'm unable to feel pleasure. I just... haven't really noticed if I am or not.
Do you feel like things that used to give you pleasure no longer do?

I don't know if they *no longer* do, it's just... I'm not really tracking that sort of thing right now. Like, I don't sit down and think, "Am I enjoying this?" 

I used to do that, though, when I was choreographing more often. You have to be so hyper-aware of how a movement feels, how it translates to an audience. I was working on this contemporary piece last fall, and the studio we rented had these gorgeous floor-to-ceiling mirrors. But the floors were terrible. They were supposed to be sprung wood, but I swear there were dead spots all over the room. One of my dancers actually tweaked her ankle on a jump because the floor had zero give in that one specific corner. We had to ice it for twenty minutes while the rest of the cast just sat around marking the choreography with their hands. Have you ever watched dancers mark? It looks completely ridiculous if you don't know what they're doing. Just a bunch of people sitting in a circle, twitching their fingers and nodding aggressively to the music. The music for that piece was this really intense instrumental track with a lot of heavy cello. I actually reached out to the composer on Instagram to ask if we could use it, and he was incredibly nice about it. He lives in Iceland, which is somewhere I've always wanted to go. I saw this documentary about the hot springs there, and they look amazing, but apparently, they smell strongly of sulfur. Like rotten eggs. I don't know if I could relax in a pool that smells like breakfast gone wrong, you know? My old roommate used to make hard-boiled eggs every morning, and she would always forget them on the stove until the water boiled away and the shells started cracking. The smell would linger in the apartment for days. I had to buy so many of those plug-in air fresheners, but they just made the place smell like lavender-scented sulfur. 

So... yeah, I guess I haven't really noticed if things give me pleasure anymore. I'm just kind of going through the motions.
Do you feel like you're unable to find joy or pleasure in anything at all?

I mean... joy is a strong word. I don't really know if I'm finding joy in anything, but I'm not really looking for it either, I guess. 

I was looking for my keys this morning, though, and I realized I haven't seen my favorite keychain in weeks. It's this little enameled ballet slipper that one of my students gave me at a recital a few years ago. She was this tiny, fiery little thing—maybe seven years old? She refused to wear her hair in a traditional bun and always insisted on these elaborate French braids. Her mom was a hairstylist, so they always looked perfect, but they were a nightmare when we had to fit headpieces for the spring showcase. We were doing this variation on A Midsummer Night's Dream, and all the little fairies had to wear these stiff, wire flower crowns. They kept sliding off everyone's heads because the wire was too heavy for the bobby pins to hold. I ended up having to hot-glue felt strips to the inside of all twenty crowns the night before dress rehearsal. I burned my thumb so badly on the glue gun that I had a blister for a week. Have you ever done that? Hot glue is no joke. It sticks to your skin and just keeps burning while you try to peel it off. I had to keep my hand in a bowl of ice water while I was giving notes to the lighting designer. He was this older guy who always wore socks with sandals, even in the middle of winter. He claimed it was a European fashion statement, but I'm pretty sure he just had bad circulation. He was brilliant with the gels, though. He made the stage look like it was actually glowing during the finale. 

But, um... yeah, I don't know about joy. I just haven't really been paying attention to whether I feel it or not.
Do you feel like you have less energy than you used to?

I mean, yeah, I guess I do. I feel totally wiped out after doing just small things. Like, I'll answer one email to a dancer about scheduling, or just take a shower with this stupid ankle brace on, and I'm exhausted. And lying down doesn't really recharge me, either. 

I was actually lying down yesterday afternoon, trying to rest, and I started thinking about the ceiling fan in my bedroom. It has a slight wobble to it, you know? Like it's just a tiny bit off-balance. I kept watching it spin and wondering if it was going to fly off the ceiling and crash into my bed. I read this article once about how ceiling fans are actually really heavy, and if they aren't anchored to the joists properly, they can cause serious structural damage if they fall. My upstairs neighbor actually had a leak in his bathroom last year, and the water seeped all the way down into my living room ceiling. It left this awful brown water stain right above my couch. The landlord said he was going to paint over it, but he used the wrong shade of white, so now there's just a bright, stark white square in the middle of this slightly off-white ceiling. It drives me crazy every time I look at it. I tried moving the couch so I wouldn't be staring directly up at it when I sit down, but my living room is so small that the couch really only fits against that one wall. I bought it at this vintage furniture store downtown. It's a mid-century modern piece, real velvet, in this deep emerald green. It's beautiful, but it is a magnet for cat hair. I don't even own a cat, but my friend brings hers over sometimes when she visits, and I swear I'm still finding orange fur on the cushions weeks later. 

So, yeah... I'm just really tired. Like, all the time.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

Yeah, I think so. My rehearsal clothes have been hanging a lot looser lately. When I was, you know, really buzzing with all those choreography ideas a while back, I would just completely skip meals and not even notice. I'd be in the studio for like ten hours straight. And now... I don't know, food just tastes like cardboard. 

I actually tried to make a sandwich yesterday, just turkey and cheese, but the bread was so dry. I bought it from that bakery down the street, the one that always has a line out the door on Sunday mornings. They make these incredible almond croissants, but you have to get there by 8 AM or they sell out. I went there once with my sister when she visited from Chicago. She's obsessed with bakeries because she's trying to start her own catering business, but she only wants to cater for dogs. Like, gourmet dog food. She spent three hours telling me about the nutritional benefits of sweet potatoes for golden retrievers. She has a golden retriever named Barnaby, and he's terrified of balloons. We had a birthday party for him last year, and someone brought a mylar balloon shaped like a bone, and he hid under the dining table for the entire afternoon. It was a really nice table, too—solid oak, belonged to our grandmother. She used to polish it every Sunday with this lemon oil that smelled so strong it would give me a headache. 

But um, yeah. My clothes are definitely looser. I just don't have much of an appetite right now.
Do you find yourself moving or speaking more slowly than you used to?

I think so, yeah. It's like... even just crossing the studio to pick up my notebook feels so slowed down. Like my body is moving through wet sand instead of music. 

I actually dropped my notebook the other day because my grip just felt so weak. It's this beautiful leather-bound one that I got at a craft fair in the park last summer. The guy who made it had this huge beard and was telling me all about how he sources the leather from a sustainable farm in upstate New York. He had all these different dyes, and he explained the whole tanning process, which honestly sounded kind of gross when you get into the chemical part of it. But the notebook is gorgeous. It has this embossed compass rose on the cover. I used to be obsessed with compasses when I was a kid because my dad was a surveyor. He had all these antique brass instruments in his office, and he’d never let me touch them because the oils on my fingers would tarnish the metal. He was really particular about his things. He used to arrange his vinyl records by the exact release date, not just the year, but the actual day they came out. He had this massive collection of 70s prog rock. I tried listening to it once, but the songs are like twenty minutes long and they change time signatures so many times you can't even tap your foot to them. 

But yeah... moving feels really heavy. Just really slow and heavy right now.
Do you find yourself having trouble concentrating or making decisions?

I don't know, maybe? I guess I haven't really noticed having trouble with that specifically. I mean, my mind just feels kind of blank a lot of the time, so there isn't much to concentrate on anyway. 

I did try to read a book yesterday, just to have something to do while I was resting my ankle. It was this mystery novel my friend lent me, the one with the cat hair on her clothes. She's really into those cozy mysteries where the detective is always a baker or a librarian or something. This one was about a woman who owns a yarn shop in a small town in Maine, and she solves murders using clues she finds in knitting patterns. It sounds ridiculous, but my friend swears by them. She actually knits, too. She made me this huge, chunky scarf for my birthday last year, but she used this wool that is so incredibly itchy I can't even wear it. I feel bad because she spent weeks on it, and she kept texting me updates about her progress, sending pictures of the different color blocks. She chose these really bright neon colors—pink and yellow and lime green—which is totally not my style. I usually wear black or gray, especially in the studio, because it's just easier to see the lines of the body when you're choreographing. Plus, black doesn't show sweat as much. I used to buy all my dancewear from this one specific catalog, but they went out of business a few years ago. It was so sad, they had the best leotards with these intricate strappy backs. 

But um... yeah, I don't think I'm having trouble making decisions or anything. I just don't have much to decide right now.
Do you often feel guilty or blame yourself for things?

I mean, yeah, constantly. I keep replaying the cancelled performances in my head, over and over. I just keep telling myself I let everyone down—the dancers, the funders, the whole community. Even though people have actually been way kinder about it than I deserve. 

It's just hard because the funders, especially, they really took a chance on me. One of the main grants we got was from this local arts council, and the woman who runs it, Brenda, she was so supportive. She actually came to one of our early rehearsals. She brought this huge tray of muffins from a bakery near her house. They were those massive Costco-style muffins, you know? Like, bigger than your fist. She brought blueberry, poppyseed, and double chocolate. I didn't eat any because I was in the middle of that really intense phase where I was just buzzing and working non-stop, but the dancers loved them. One of my lead dancers, Mark, he ate two of the double chocolate ones. He has this crazy metabolism where he can just eat whatever he wants and never gain an ounce. He told me he grew up on a farm in Wisconsin and used to eat an entire box of cereal for breakfast before doing chores. He said they had dairy cows, mostly Holsteins, the black and white ones. He showed me a picture once of him as a kid trying to ride one of the calves. It was hilarious, he had this bright red bowl cut and overalls. His mom actually cut his hair herself until he was in high school, which is wild because now he's so particular about his hair. He goes to this super expensive salon downtown where they give you a glass of champagne while you wait. I went there once, but the stylist talked so much about her cat's digestive issues that I never went back. 

But yeah... I just feel terrible about letting everyone down with the cancellations. It's really heavy on my mind.
Have you been having any thoughts of hurting yourself?

No, no I haven't had any thoughts like that. I mean, my ankle hurts enough already, I definitely don't want to add any more pain to the situation. 

I've been going to physical therapy for it twice a week, actually. The clinic is over on 4th street, right next to this amazing little bakery that sells these incredible almond croissants. The physical therapist, Dave, he's always telling me I need to avoid sugar because it causes joint inflammation, but he drinks like four huge cups of coffee while I'm doing my resistance band exercises. He has this mug that says "World's Okayest Golfer" on it. He was telling me how he went to Myrtle Beach last spring for a golf trip with his college buddies, but it rained the entire time, so they just stayed in the rental house playing poker and watching old action movies. He said they watched Die Hard three times. I've actually never seen Die Hard. My brother loves it, though. He watches it every Christmas because he insists it's a Christmas movie, which is this whole exhausting debate he brings up every year. He even bought this ugly Christmas sweater with Bruce Willis's face on it and wore it to my parents' house last year. My mom was so annoyed because she wanted everyone to dress nicely for a family photo. She had hired this professional photographer who brought all these huge umbrellas and lighting rigs right into our living room, and the guy kept tripping over the rug. It's this antique Persian rug my grandmother left us, and the edges are all frayed because her cat used to use it as a scratching post... 

But um, no. No thoughts of hurting myself at all.
Do you find yourself fidgeting or having trouble sitting still?

Well, sitting still isn't really the issue. It's actually the opposite right now. I just... I feel so heavy. Like, recently, even just crossing the studio to pick up my notebook feels incredibly slowed down, like my body is moving through wet sand instead of music. 

Which is so frustrating because I usually have this very specific notebook I use for choreography. It's this Moleskine one with dotted pages, not lined. I hate lined paper for notes, it feels too restrictive. I actually buy them in bulk from this little stationery store in my old neighborhood. The guy who owns it, Mr. Henderson, he always gives me a discount because I used to buy my pens there when I was in college. He has this massive collection of vintage fountain pens displayed in a glass case by the register. He told me once that he bought an entire estate sale lot just to get this one specific 1920s Waterman pen. He spent like three hours cleaning the dried ink out of the nib with this tiny little ultrasonic cleaner. It was fascinating, honestly. He showed me how the gold nibs flex differently depending on how much pressure you apply. My grandfather used to use a fountain pen. He had this beautiful cursive handwriting, the kind they don't teach in schools anymore. He used to write me these long letters when I was away at summer dance intensive in New York. The intensive was at this old building near Lincoln Center, and the elevators were always broken, so we had to walk up six flights of stairs every morning. By the time we got to the studio, we were already sweating. There was this one girl there, Chloe, who used to bring these elaborate bento box lunches her mom made... 

But yeah, no fidgeting. Just feeling really, really slow and heavy when I try to move.
Do you feel like your movements or speech have slowed down significantly?

Yeah, exactly like I was just saying a second ago. It's really noticeable. My movements are just... significantly slower. Like I mentioned, even just crossing the studio feels like dragging myself through wet sand instead of moving to the music. 

Speaking of sand, my sister actually just got back from a beach trip to Destin. Have you been? The sand there is supposed to be super fine, like powdered sugar. She brought back this little glass bottle filled with it, layered with these tiny pink seashells. She collects seashells. Her whole guest bathroom is ocean-themed, which is honestly a little tacky if you ask me, but she loves it. She even has this shower curtain with giant sea turtles on it. She found it at Target on clearance. Target always has the best clearance section, especially right after a holiday. I went there the day after Halloween last year and bought like four bags of those miniature Reese's cups. The ones shaped like pumpkins? They always taste better than the regular cups, I swear it's because the peanut butter to chocolate ratio is different. My old roommate used to put them in the freezer. She was obsessed with freezing all her candy, even gummy bears, which just makes them impossible to chew. She actually chipped a tooth on a frozen Milk Dud once and had to go to this emergency dentist who had an office in a strip mall next to a dry cleaner. The dry cleaner always smelled heavily of chemicals, like that really sharp PERC smell... 

But yeah, to answer your question, everything just feels really slowed down right now.
Do you feel like you're at a point where you can't imagine things getting better?

Well, yeah, I guess so. What brings me in is that I’ve been waking up with this heavy, hollow sadness, like the studio lights are on but there’s no music in me anymore. It's just this constant feeling that nothing is ever going to change. 

I used to wake up so early, you know? Like 5:30 AM, before the sun was even up, just to get to the studio and stretch before anyone else got there. The morning light coming through those big arched windows was just perfect. The studio is in this old converted warehouse downtown, right next to a place that roasts their own coffee beans. The smell of the roasting coffee would drift in through the vents around 7 AM every day. The guy who runs the roastery, Mateo, he has this massive, gorgeous Bernese Mountain Dog named Barnaby who just sleeps on a rug by the door all day. People literally come in just to pet the dog. Mateo told me once that Barnaby eats like four cups of this super expensive grain-free salmon kibble every day. I tried giving my cat salmon once, but she threw it up all over my favorite armchair. It's this vintage velvet wingback chair I found at a flea market in Brooklyn like ten years ago. The guy selling it wanted two hundred dollars, but I talked him down to eighty because there was a small tear on the back. I ended up sewing it up myself with this heavy-duty upholstery thread I bought at a craft store. The craft store was having a massive clearance sale because they were closing down, which was so sad. I bought like ten skeins of merino wool yarn thinking I was going to learn how to knit a sweater, but I only ever made a very lopsided scarf that I ended up giving to my niece. She's seven, so she didn't care that it was crooked. She just loved that it was bright purple. Her whole bedroom is purple, actually. Even the ceiling...

But, um, to answer your question, yeah. I just feel this deep sadness and I can't really picture it lifting.
Do you think your current state is the worst it's been?

I don't know if it's the absolute worst it's ever been, honestly. It's hard to compare. I just know it feels pretty bad right now. 

It's funny trying to measure things like that, isn't it? Like, how do you quantify "worst"? It reminds me of when we were trying to score this contemporary piece last spring, and the composer kept asking me to rate the intensity of the climax on a scale of one to ten. He was this brilliant guy, but very numbers-driven. He actually used to be an actuary before he went back to school for music composition. He said the risk assessment models he used for insurance companies actually helped him understand musical tension and release. He worked for this huge firm in Chicago, right in the Loop. My cousin lived in Chicago for a while, right off the blue line. She used to complain about the noise all the time, but I always thought the sound of the train was kind of rhythmic. Almost like a metronome. She had this tiny apartment with exposed brick walls that were always shedding red dust on her furniture. She had to buy this special HEPA vacuum cleaner just to keep up with it. It was one of those Dyson ones that looks like a spaceship. I always wanted a Dyson, but they're so expensive. I ended up getting a refurbished Shark on Amazon Prime Day instead. It works okay, but the cord is just slightly too short to reach the far corner of my living room, which drives me crazy because I have this large fiddle leaf fig tree there that drops dry leaves... 

But yeah, I don't know if this is the worst it's ever been. It's just... really heavy right now.
Do you think you might be experiencing a major depressive episode?

I mean, I don't really know what to call it. I'm not a doctor, you know? I just know I feel empty and slow. 

It's kind of like trying to label a style of dance. People always want to put things in boxes—is it modern, is it contemporary, is it lyrical? I had this one student, Clara, who was obsessed with definitions. She'd stop in the middle of a combination and ask, "But is this technically a Graham contraction or more of a Horton release?" She was only fourteen, but she read all these dance history books. Her mom was a librarian at the county library, the one over on Elm Street with the really cool mid-century modern architecture. They have these huge glass panels that look out into a courtyard with a fountain. The fountain was broken for like three years, though. It just sat there collecting algae and dead leaves until the city finally got a grant to fix it. They hired this local sculptor to redesign the centerpiece, and he made this abstract bronze thing that looks kind of like a flock of birds taking off, or maybe a twisted up tree root. It's supposed to represent community growth, I think. He used to come into this cafe I liked, always covered in metal dust and smelling like welding gas. He ordered the same thing every day—a large black coffee and an almond croissant. The almond croissants there were amazing, they had this thick layer of marzipan inside. I tried making marzipan at home once for my mom's birthday cake. She loves anything with almonds. But it turned out super gritty because I didn't use the right kind of powdered sugar. I guess there's a difference between regular powdered sugar and the extra-fine kind they use in bakeries...

But anyway, to your question... I don't really know the medical term for what I'm going through. I just know it feels awful.

Hi... well, what brings me in is that I’ve just been waking up with this really heavy, hollow sadness. It's... it's like the studio lights are on, but there is no music in me anymore, you know?

I bought like ten skeins of merino wool yarn thinking I was going to learn how to knit a sweater, but I only ever made a very lopsided scarf that I ended up giving to my niece. She's seven, so she didn't care that it was crooked. She just loved that it was bright purple. Her whole bedroom is purple, actually. Even the ceiling...

But, um, to answer your question, yeah. I just feel this deep sadness and I can't really picture it lifting.

doctor.intent: Determine the severity of depressive episode
doctor.question: Do you think your current state is the worst it's been?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the severity of the current depressive state, which does not map to a specific new symptom in the profile.

patient.answer:
I don't know if it's the absolute worst it's ever been, honestly. It's hard to compare. I just know it feels pretty bad right now. 

It's funny trying to measure things like that, isn't it? Like, how do you quantify "worst"? It reminds me of when we were trying to score this contemporary piece last spring, and the composer kept asking me to rate the intensity of the climax on a scale of one to ten. He was this brilliant guy, but very numbers-driven. He actually used to be an actuary before he went back to school for music composition. He said the risk assessment models he used for insurance companies actually helped him understand musical tension and release. He worked for this huge firm in Chicago, right in the Loop. My cousin lived in Chicago for a while, right off the blue line. She used to complain about the noise all the time, but I always thought the sound of the train was kind of rhythmic. Almost like a metronome. She had this tiny apartment with exposed brick walls that were always shedding red dust on her furniture. She had to buy this special HEPA vacuum cleaner just to keep up with it. It was one of those Dyson ones that looks like a spaceship. I always wanted a Dyson, but they're so expensive. I ended up getting a refurbished Shark on Amazon Prime Day instead. It works okay, but the cord is just slightly too short to reach the far corner of my living room, which drives me crazy because I have this large fiddle leaf fig tree there that drops dry leaves... 

But yeah, I don't know if this is the worst it's ever been. It's just... really heavy right now.

doctor.intent: Determine the severity of the patient's depression
doctor.question: Do you think you might be experiencing a major depressive episode?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking for the patient's opinion on whether they are experiencing a major depressive episode, which is a diagnostic question and does not directly map to any specific symptom or duration in the profile.

patient.answer:
I mean, I don't really know what to call it. I'm not a doctor, you know? I just know I feel empty and slow. 

It's kind of like trying to label a style of dance. People always want to put things in boxes—is it modern, is it contemporary, is it lyrical? I had this one student, Clara, who was obsessed with definitions. She'd stop in the middle of a combination and ask, "But is this technically a Graham contraction or more of a Horton release?" She was only fourteen, but she read all these dance history books. Her mom was a librarian at the county library, the one over on Elm Street with the really cool mid-century modern architecture. They have these huge glass panels that look out into a courtyard with a fountain. The fountain was broken for like three years, though. It just sat there collecting algae and dead leaves until the city finally got a grant to fix it. They hired this local sculptor to redesign the centerpiece, and he made this abstract bronze thing that looks kind of like a flock of birds taking off, or maybe a twisted up tree root. It's supposed to represent community growth, I think. He used to come into this cafe I liked, always covered in metal dust and smelling like welding gas. He ordered the same thing every day—a large black coffee and an almond croissant. The almond croissants there were amazing, they had this thick layer of marzipan inside. I tried making marzipan at home once for my mom's birthday cake. She loves anything with almonds. But it turned out super gritty because I didn't use the right kind of powdered sugar. I guess there's a difference between regular powdered sugar and the extra-fine kind they use in bakeries...

But anyway, to your question... I don't really know the medical term for what I'm going through. I just know it feels awful.

These symptoms align with the diagnostic criteria for a Major Depressive Disorder, Single Episode.
